summary: Codex 0.155.0-alpha.16.3 has no agents field in the Chohogi plugin manifest schema. codex plugin add reports Chohogi installed and enabled, but ~/.codex/config.toml contained no [agents.*] entries. The five role TOMLs therefore had no persistent Codex loader registration. Prior replay used --codex-role-config, which proved a per-run override only.

topic: Codex role absence after plugin installation
observations: The documented Codex install command completes without editing agents.* config entries.
The plugin manifest has no role slot and cannot express the five role TOMLs.
Chohogi documents the required registrations but labels them user-action and has no installer or doctor that detects this capability gap.
A role is a declared active runtime capability, so installed-but-unspawnable is an installation/discovery failure for the advertised harness capability.
options: Classify it as a Chohogi installation/discovery defect while preserving the native Codex schema limitation
selected: Classify it as a Chohogi installation/discovery defect while preserving the native Codex schema limitation
rationale: The native plugin schema explains why plugin add cannot do the registration. It does not justify reporting a role-capable Codex installation as healthy when no role is discoverable. The prior user-action classification hid that gap and the replay override masked it.
reviewTrigger: A native Codex plugin lifecycle API that can safely declare or install agent config entries, or a fresh live session contradicting the absence/discovery evidence.

summary: Under the user’s explicit authorization, added all five canonical Chohogi role config_file registrations to ~/.codex/config.toml. Python tomllib parsed the full file and each path exists.

The earlier configuration-change event incorrectly said Python tomllib parsed config.toml. This runtime has no tomllib module. The claim is withdrawn; only exact section/path checks have passed so far. Fresh Codex replay is the authoritative parser/discovery check.

Fresh paid Codex sessions, with no --codex-role-config override, spawned all five registered Chohogi agent types and each completed a read-only README task with ROLE_OK: critical_reviewer, evidence_scout, implementation_worker, final_reviewer, debugger. Every spawn requested gpt-5.6-luna with low reasoning effort.

A paid seven-scenario fresh Codex replay on gpt-5.6-luna without a role override passed five non-delegation scenarios and failed both delegation scenarios because the parent session did not call spawn_agent. This is distinct from role registration: direct agent_type spawns all succeeded afterward.

topic: Smallest durable repair for Codex role installation
observations: Native codex plugin add has no lifecycle mechanism or manifest field for agent registration.
The five config entries make roles usable in this host, proven by live agent_type spawns.
A manual README block can be missed; a replay -c override can mask persistent install failure.
Automatic mutation of personal config during plugin add is not available through the observed native interface.
options: Add a Chohogi doctor/setup adapter that detects missing registrations and applies the canonical entries only when explicitly run
selected: Add a Chohogi doctor/setup adapter that detects missing registrations and applies the canonical entries only when explicitly run
rationale: It closes the false-installed state and provides a concrete, idempotent activation action without pretending the native plugin installer can mutate personal configuration. The current user-authorized registration repairs this host; the adapter prevents the same hidden gap for later installations.
reviewTrigger: Codex adds an official agent-registration field or install lifecycle hook, or an adapter cannot preserve unrelated config safely.

summary: Causal trace and defect classification recorded.
Five canonical config_file entries added under explicit user authorization.
Fresh direct agent_type spawns prove discovery without a per-run override.
Paid seven-scenario replay completed; two parent-policy delegation failures recorded separately from role discovery.
Selected an explicit doctor/setup adapter as the durable repair; implementation remains a new source change.

Confirmed installation defect and repaired this host: five missing config registrations were the reason Codex roles could not be invoked. All five canonical roles now spawn in fresh paid gpt-5.6-luna sessions without a run-only override.
feedback: The feedback document classified F4 as user-action. The live evidence shows that classification concealed a Chohogi installation/discovery defect: native schema limits explain the mechanism, but not the advertised capability gap.
remainingRisk: The seven-scenario replay passed five non-delegation cases but failed both policy-driven delegation cases because the parent session chose not to spawn. Native Codex plugin add still cannot write agents.* itself. A doctor/setup adapter is selected but not yet implemented.

summary: Corrective source work: added tooling/codex-role-setup.py. It detects the five canonical [agents.<role>] registrations and --apply appends only missing config_file blocks, preserving existing text. Added a test that starts with a config containing unrelated model data, verifies all five registrations, and verifies a second --apply is byte-identical.

The two failed review replays do not refute registration: direct fresh agent_type spawns succeeded. Their prompts requested an independent review but did not cause the parent to create a scoped-delegation contract; Codex therefore performed the review directly under its no-implicit-delegation instruction. The scenario must encode the delegation contract before it can test model-card/profile behavior.

summary: Found and repaired a false delegation observation: Codex rollout parser treated /session internal calls as agent_type values. It now ignores empty and slash-prefixed agent_type values. The raw exec transcript proves a spawn_agent tool call occurred, but its streamed item omits agent_type/model fields; current replay cannot prove those fields from this host transcript and reports that limitation instead of inventing a role.

Full remaining-defect verification: project document registry, model policy, semantic assurance, and source layout passed. Functional assurance failed because tooling/codex-role-setup.py is an uncovered active command; homeostasis policy failed only because it consumes that failed assurance verifier. F11, F16, F17, F20, F21, and F22 remain confirmed by current source plus prior mutation/replay evidence. F2, F3, F10, F12, F14, F23, F24, and F25 remain open pending their stated host observation or decision.

F27 resolved. The observations came from different replay runs and two different evidence channels. The original seven-scenario replay had no parsed registered-role delegation. The later explicit scoped-delegation run contains a completed collab_tool_call spawn_agent, wait, close_agent, and reviewer handoff. The apparent /session roles were rollout internal calls, not agents. The raw collab stream omits agent_type/model fields, so it proves creation and completion but not those fields.

The installed cache initially lacked two newly added source tooling files; running codex plugin add chohogi@chohogi-marketplace refreshed the cache and both paths then existed.
